Buying meat cheaply is pretty easy, if you know what you are doing.

There are several options.

Buy lower grade meat

Get shiitier meat for a lower price, but you lose quality. It is a trade off.

Keep in mind, poultry and beef both have grading standards, whereas pork does not (but not all pork is created equal).

It is entirely up to you, but I would avoid this option.

Buying from universities

Sounds kind of odd, right? But larger universities that have meat science degrees usually run small butcher shops.

Example:http://www.ans.iastate.edu/section/meat/?pg=order

They are usually doing at cost, or close to cost. It is a viable option, google your local university to see if they have a meat sciences program.

Buy markdowns

If there is too much processed, we have to mark it down to avoid throwing things away. They are done near the end of the date on the package. If they do their markdowns first thing, swing buy on your way to work. Buy while it is cheap and stock up.

Ask politely about the markdown policy at your local grocery store. Some of the stuff might be a little janky looking.

If you're nice and form a relationship with the local store, they will hook you up with deals, and help you out.
